note: 2026-11-14 - 'The Devious Tactics of Misleading Advertising | The Kevin Trudeau Show' (Rumble v4rcljt). HEALTH INSIDE OTHER EPISODES by weekly agent: this episode is about advertising/media, not titled health, but Kevin plays real vintage drug ads inside it. Checked this episode's other promising stretches hard against what WB has already posted/planned: the 'three levels of organic' label bit (00:07:36-00:08:42) is a duplicate of ep_v4ki1z0_r2/WHAT-YOUR-FOOD-LABEL-IS-HIDING; the cinnamon/talcum-powder 'I was right' list (00:29:58+) says 'cancer' and 'almost cure diabetes' back to back and is really about Kevin's own vindication, not viewer-usable info; the psychiatric-medication/mass-shootings stretch (01:13:25+) says 'suicidal' repeatedly and is off the health lane into violence. Skipped all of those, plus the sexist vintage-ad reel (00:14:08-00:16:44, off-lane) and the 7-up-for-babies ad (00:12:18 on) because it immediately runs into 'stupid mother... stupid, ignorant, uneducated mother' and then 'idiot/idiotic' - harsh words anywhere in the clip refuse it. One clean arc survived: the cocaine toothache-drops ad, which stops cleanly right before the 7-up ad's harsh words begin.

clips.send: A dad sends this to his buddy mid-joke about 'the good old days': anger that a real company sold an addictive drug as children's medicine and knew it.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau holds up a real old pharmacy ad: toothache drops from Lloyd Manufacturing, marketed as an instant fix for pain.

The active ingredient was cocaine. It wasn't hidden - doctors and the manufacturer both knew, and sold it anyway, until cocaine itself became illegal.

His point: the shelf has always been where the selling happens, not the proof. A product can look medical and still be built to keep you buying.

Next time a label promises a quick fix, read what's actually inside it, not just what the box claims.

The names on the shelf change. The trick doesn't.
